gallery.filename: Porth Hellick Pool, St. Mary's - geograph.org.uk - 934736.jpg
gallery.title: File:Porth Hellick Pool, St. Mary's - geograph.org.uk - 934736.jpg
gallery.description: Porth Hellick Pool, St. Mary's The view from one of the hides of this SSSI (Site of Special Scientific Interest). A heron is keeping quite still in the reeds (left of centre). In addition to its importance as the largest area of freshwater on St. Mary's, and catchments for drinking water, it is also popular with waders and wild fowl. Higher Moors and this pool are nationally famous for rare vagrant birds and also less common passage migrants such as Spotted Crake or Jack Snipe.

gallery.title: File:Porth Hellick in 1972 - geograph.org.uk - 1572549.jpg
gallery.description: Porth Hellick in 1972 This is a view over Porth Hellick from the higher ground to the east. Porth Hellick is an enclosed bay. Here the tide is fairly will up. At low tide there is an expanse of rocks and seaweed. The fine sandy beach to the right is a nesting site for Ringed Plovers. Fortunately, most of these will have hatched their eggs before the main tourist invasion in high summer.

gallery.filename: Porth Hellick and the Loaded Camel rock, St Mary's, Scilly - geograph.org.uk - 1607574.jpg
gallery.title: File:Porth Hellick and the Loaded Camel rock, St Mary's, Scilly - geograph.org.uk - 1607574.jpg
gallery.description: Porth Hellick and the Loaded Camel rock, St Mary's, Scilly. This was taken from Porth Hellick Down, to the north of the bay. The tide is fairly well up, so that just the sandy beach is visible. To the right of the bay is the Higher Moors Pool. The seat 1607571 is behind the Loaded Camel Rock seen in front of the bay. The view here, in 2007, is not far from that taken in 1972 1572549.

gallery.filename: Seat at Porth Hellick, St Mary's, Scilly - geograph.org.uk - 1607571.jpg
gallery.title: File:Seat at Porth Hellick, St Mary's, Scilly - geograph.org.uk - 1607571.jpg
gallery.description: Seat at Porth Hellick, St Mary's, Scilly One of the great features of the Isles of Scilly is the abundance of seats or other resting places. This is a boon for those like me with arthritic knees. This seat, at the junction of the coast footpath, and the one to the Higher Moors, has the added benefit of a good view over Porth Hellick.
